## 6. HEARINGS, PETITIONS, MEMORIALS, AND REMONSTRANCES

Council will hold public hearings on National Grid petitions to install new poles and underground conduits

**321-26** 

Petition: Massachusetts Electric Company dba National Grid and Verizon New

England, Inc. Plan No. 31120327

· National Grid to install 1 Sole Owned pole on Pearl Street beginning at a point approximately 145 feet south of the centerline of the intersection of Medford Street and Pearl Street, in front of 392 Pearl Street. National Grid to install new sole owned pole 354-50-1 for future riser pole. · National Grid to install 1 Joint Owned pole on Pearl Street beginning at a point approximately 145 feet south of the centerline of the intersection of Medford Street and Pearl Street, in front of 363 Pearl Street. National Grid to install new joint owned pole 354-50 for mid-span tap.

· National Grid to install underground facilities on Pearl Street beginning at a point approximately 20 feet north of the centerline of the intersection of Medford Street and Pearl Street, in front of 315 Medford Street, and continuing approximately 205 feet in a south direction, ending in front of 392 Pearl Street. National Grid is petitioning to install two 5-inch ducts from existing MH 605 south approximately 205 feet to a new riser pole on the east side of Pearl Street.

(Hearings Required)

Attachments: Pearl Street - New Sole Owned Pole Petition

Pearl Street - New Joint Owned Pole Petition

Pearl Street - Underground Conduit Petition

Abutters 316 Medford Street (Pearl St)

Hearing Notice Pearl Street Petitions

Zein Jumaa from National Grid was in attendance to speak on behalf of the petition. This petition was filed due to existing conduit on Pearl Street no longer being in compliance with regulations regarding clearance of water and cable lines. There is existing conduit in the area from the manhole to the pole but the conduit has to be rerouted to the other side of the street so the electric conduits are not running too close to underground water and cable lines.

Councillor O'Malley clarified with Mr. Jumaa that National Grid does not have a conflict with MWRA so much as it is the reverse and perhaps the Council should be calling in MWRA to discuss their underground needs. This is not just an MWRA concern; National Grid has their own safety standards that do not allow these lines to run too close to a water source. Mr. Jumaa explained that MWRA has a proposed project to update old water lines that cannot begin until the electric conduits are moved, which is the need for this petition.

No member of the public came to speak either in favor or opposition to this petition during the hearing.

Councillor Condon had further questions about the proposed work as outlined in the petition and requested it be tabled until he could meet with a National Grid representative on-site.

A motion was made by Councillor Condon, seconded by Councillor Simonelli, that the Petition be tabled. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

headline: Council enrolled data center moratorium ordinance, approved CPC funding for Trafton Park and Emmanuel Baptist Church, and tabled a National Grid pole petition.
summary: The Council approved the Consent Agenda, placed four mayoral appointments on file, and referred several petitions to the License Committee and ordinances to the Rules & Ordinance Committee. It tabled a National Grid petition on Pearl Street, ordained the Sign Control ordinance, and enrolled and ordained the Data Centers ordinance (Paper 276-26) by an 11-0 vote. The Council also adopted FY2027 appropriation orders, CPC funding of $50,000 for Trafton Park and $100,000 for Emmanuel Baptist Church, referred three zoning ordinances to joint Planning Board and Rules and Ordinance Committee sessions, and voted 11-0 to enter Executive Session to discuss Barkosky v. Malden Police Department litigation.
